fact_overrides.notes: https://github.com/cortexkit/anthropic-auth/blob/a9b4c35b1ed5aef217d29e6dc699d60589b0c9e2/packages/core/src/model-capabilities.ts marks id 'claude-opus-5-5' serverSideFallback: true. The page names no dated snapshot ids. Server-side fallback is in beta on the Claude API and on Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), so the fact is not projected onto alias routes that reach the model another way. Live check 2026-10-28 about 16:05Z: a Claude subscription (OAuth) request to claude-opus-5-5 with fallbacks set to default and the server-side-fallback-2026-07-01 beta returned HTTP 200 and handed off mid-reply to claude-opus-4-8 (response sha256 fdec66cc43c189769f8571c01e861be2370abc82729f5791733b89dfb5f39259).
fact_overrides.quote: "Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Fable 5, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Opus 5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, and Claude Haiku 5.5 include safety classifiers that can decline a request." "Set the `fallbacks` parameter to the string `"default"` and send the `server-side-fallback-2026-07-01` beta header. The API then applies the requested model's server-defined default routing, which selects a recommended fallback model based on the refusal category the classifier reports, so refused requests are served without you maintaining a model list as recommendations change." "Claude Haiku 5.5 has no server-side fallback: with `fallbacks: "default"`, a declined request stays declined, and a list of fallback models returns a 400 error."
fact_overrides.reason: models.dev publishes no server-side fallback field. Anthropic's page names six models with safety classifiers, Claude Opus 5.5 among them, states the fallback generally for the Claude API, and excludes only Haiku 5.5. anthropic-auth's model table (a9b4c35) also marks this model true. This is a reading of the page's structure, not a sentence naming Claude Opus 5.5.

quota_value.basis: List-price value of in-scope tokens divided by (weekly-window quota points used x fee per point), fee per point = monthly price x 7/30 / 100. Pooled across 5 accounts. Daily rows 2026-10-01..10-09, each covering the trailing 7 days. Excludes the 09-25/26 rows (85-88x), recorded before the series settled. Reads 1-2% high, because usage between the last reading and a reset is lost.
quota_value.token_mix: Agentic coding, 98.5% cache read, 1.3% cache write, 0.13% output, 0.07% reasoning, 0.01% input, over 44.9B tokens. A chat-heavy mix would read differently.

quota_value.refusal_reason: No Max 5x account is held, so astrocyte has measured none; the operator can state a figure.
No AI Ultra 5x account is measured yet; astrocyte has no Antigravity multiplier readings. The operator can state a figure.
No Kimi Code account is measured yet; astrocyte has no Kimi readings. The operator can state a figure.
No Muse Code account is measured yet; the operator's login is new and astrocyte has no Meta readings. The operator can state a figure.

prices.refusal_reason: "pro" is an API plan string, not a vendor tier name. OpenAI publishes Pro 100 ($100), Pro 200 ($200) and Pro 500 ($500); the API plan string does not establish which an account holds, so this key cannot carry one price. The tier rows are openai/pro_100, openai/pro_200 and openai/pro_500; the account's tier is a fact about the account.

quota_value.refusal_reason: Pro 100 is unmeasured: the one account possibly on it is not configured in astrocyte and its tier is unconfirmed.

quota_value.basis: List-price value of in-scope tokens divided by (weekly-window quota points used x fee per point), fee per point = monthly price x 7/30 / 100, each account's points weighted by its own fee. Codex weekly ('primary') window, daily rows 2026-09-25..10-09, each covering the trailing 7 days, recorded by astrocyte under the old key name pro_20x until 10-09. Rows 09-25..10-06 pool 2 accounts on $200 Pro 200 and read 28.8-40.9x. From 10-07 a third account on $100 Pro 100 is counted too, so those rows are a pooled Pro 200 + Pro 100 figure rather than a pure Pro 200 one, and read 25.1, 23.1 and 22.8x. The series is falling, from about 40x in late September to about 23x on 10-09, so the low end is the current reading. Per-account values cannot be separated, because harness tokens carry no account. Hand-checked over two weeks to within 2%; reads 1-2% high, because usage between the last reading and a reset is lost.
quota_value.source_ref: astrocyte multiplier_observation, recomputed through spend.multiplier.recompute, read 2026-10-09
quota_value.token_mix: Agentic coding, 96.2% cache read, 3.3% input, 0.23% reasoning, 0.22% output, about 0% cache write, over 26.0B tokens.

quota_value.refusal_reason: No OpenCode Go account is measured yet; astrocyte has no Go readings. The operator can state a figure.

response.tier_vocabulary: The tier is the VENDOR'S OWN TIER NAME, never an API plan string. OpenAI's Pro 100, Pro 200 and Pro 500 are pro_100, pro_200 and pro_500 here. A consumer holding an API string must map it to a tier itself, with knowledge of the account.
response.unit_policy: US list price, monthly-billed, web subscription. An operator on an annual term, in another country, or subscribed through an app store pays something else, and this plane cannot see which.
